Every dad knows a good night of sleep is never guaranteed. But skipping training every time you’re tired just builds a cycle of inconsistency.

Here’s the framework I follow when sleep is hard to come by:

1. A PHASE VS. ONE BAD NIGHT�Ask yourself if it’s a one-off or a phase. One rough night? I still train. Not ideal, but keeping my routine matters more than comfort. If it’s been several nights in a row (sick kid, sleep regression, etc.), scale back intensity, drop volume, or take an impromptu rest day.

2. FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE�In tougher seasons (especially with newborns), 2–3 sessions a week is plenty. Fewer days = less pressure. That flexibility keeps you consistent and lets you rebuild once routines stabilize.

3. SMALL WINS�In those same seasons, aim for small wins to keep momentum. Maybe it’s not your usual number of workouts or runs — instead it’s keeping the diet dialed in or hitting a modest step count.

4. CONTROL WHAT YOU CAN�You can’t control the chaos, but you can control your response. That’s what leadership looks like at home. Learn to recognize when you need grace vs. when you’re using life as an excuse.

5. THINK BIG PICTURE�Too many guys fall off after a day or two thinking “what’s the point, I’ve already missed a few days.” Flip it: frame one bad week as 1 of 52 opportunities to put in work. No single day or week determines the outcome. The compounding interest of months does.

6. SICKNESS�Fever? 2–3 full rest days. Just a head cold? One rest day, then back to work. Know your body. Respect recovery, but don’t let comfort call the shots.

Do the above and you’re not lazy — you’re just in a season that demands more from you. What matters is that you keep showing up, even if it looks different right now.
